notes: Recomputed from supplied median AI forecast errors, 1999-2023. Z = (absolute event error - mean absolute error) / SD of signed error, separately by variable and horizon. Relevant-variable and all-variable scores are arithmetic means.

Event dates and days after the survey deadline are documentary metadata from manuscript Table 9. Deadline offsets have not been independently validated: the supplied deadline cache identifies months, not exact days. Negative offsets indicate events before the deadline.

The matching calculation uses h=0 for the Flash Crash and h=1 for every other event. The S&P downgrade therefore uses h=1 even though it preceded its survey deadline; applying the stated pre-deadline nowcast rule instead produces 0.38 for its relevant-variable score.
OLS with intercept and a dummy for survey dates after October 31, 2023; one-quarter-ahead absolute AI median errors. Conventional OLS standard errors. Significance: * p<.05; ** p<.01; *** p<.001.

Exact reproduction requires concatenating the 100-quarter baseline and 8-quarter OOS files, including duplicate 2023 survey quarters: 108 observations but 104 distinct quarters. The four post-cutoff observations are 2024Q1-Q4.

Recomputed using all 5,388 source reasoning responses, including the 80 rows named "No Name Provided". Nonexclusive case-insensitive substring matches use the exact Appendix C keyword lists. Model-based = Mechanical OR Model; Judgment-based = Policy OR Event.
Financial Crisis: 2008Q3-2009Q4; COVID-19: 2020Q1-Q4; Inflation Shock: 2022Q1-Q4; otherwise Normal. Counts and all percentages match the final paper at its printed precision.

Reconstructed with expanding OLS AR(1) models fitted separately to median human forecasts at each horizon, using only past survey observations from the baseline. Minimum training sample: two lagged pairs; rank-deficient fits are omitted. Ratios use the human MAE over its available sample; AI is restricted to dates with a human forecast, while AR(1) has fewer initial observations.

Diebold-Mariano tests use absolute losses (power=1), Harvey small-sample adjustment, two-sided t reference, and test horizon h=1 for all three forecast horizons. All 138 ratios and 69 p-values match to two decimals; significance stars are separately checked.

The original computation script is absent. This reconstruction uses supplied nowcasts: revision = forecast(t) - previous available forecast; lagged error = previous realization - previous forecast; consensus deviation = previous forecast - previous human SPF median. OLS includes an intercept and HC1 standard errors. Recalculated significance: *** p<0.01, following the original table. AI uses all raw responses, including the placeholder name, while human IDs come from supplied SPF microdata.

Published coefficients, standard errors, human observation counts and most R² values are not reproduced. AI N=5,188 is reproduced. Gaps and duplicate name-quarter observations are retained as supplied and counted in the numeric audit. The body says within-panel consensus whereas the caption says SPF consensus; the alternative within-panel estimates are also retained in the numeric file and do not reproduce the target. Alternate lag, realization-vintage and legacy-input checks did not identify the published estimator. This is an explicitly qualified reconstruction, not a confirmed replication.
